stem:
Assertion (A) : The amount of moisture in the atmosphere is associated with latitude.
Reason (R) : The ability to keep the moisture in the form of water vapour is related to temperature.
Code :

options.label: a
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: b
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

expl: Measure of water vapor present in the air is known as humidity. Humidity in the atmosphere is mainly related to temperature. So reason (R) is correct. Moisture/water vapour content decreases with an increase in latitude, that is, in tropical region humidity is 2.6%, at 500 latitude it is 0.9% and at 700 latitude it is 0.2% only. The atmosphere contains 90% moisture up to 5 km height from the ground. So the assertion (A) is also correct. Humidity is directly proportional to temperature, that is at higher temperatures air can hold more water vapour than the same amount of air at lower temperatures, so reason (R) is the correct explanation assertion (A).

stem: Humid heat is experienced in summer when the weather is :
expl: Humidity is the amount of water vapour in the air. In summer, humidity is very high therefore weather is muggy. Absolute humidity is the weight of water vapour per unit volume, usually expressed in grains per cubic foot.

options.label: d
options.text: Presence of moisture in the air

expl: Humidity is the result of the presence of moisture in the air. Significantly, the water vapour present in the atmosphere is called 'humidity'.

stem: Why are dewdrops not formed on a cloudy night?

options.label: a
options.text: Clouds absorb the radiation released from the Earth's surface.

options.label: b
options.text: Clouds reflect back the Earth's radiation.

options.label: c
options.text: The Earth's surface would have the low temperature on cloudy nights.

options.label: d
options.text: Clouds deflect the blowing wind to ground level.

expl: Dew : Dew is the water droplets formed by he condensation of water vapour on a relatively cold surface of an object. It forms when the temperature of an object drops below the dew point temperature. When there is a cloudy weather conditions, terrestrial radiation is radiated back to the earth's surface after reflection from clouds. This leads to the formation of greenhouse conditions due to which temperature on the earth's surface is relatively higher. Hence condition becomes unfavorable for the creation of dew.
